title: Research sprint friction capture — Mar 22 2026
content:
Applied ML — research sprint friction capture
Week of Mar 22, 2026 — quick running notes and action items

Attendees: Maya, Evan, Tomás, Aisha (brief), Noah (remote)
Meeting length: 35m (standup + triage)
Context: sprint focussing on compact quantization experiments (kv-prefetch + 4-bit kernels), signal from eval harness flagged small quality regressions on a subset of summarization prompts after applying KV-intent-aware quant schedule. This doc is a scratch capture of what we ran, what looked weird, and next experiments.

1) Quick summary / headline
- Experiment: 4-bit KV + asymmetric per-head scaling on osprey-13B-ql (internal name) to reduce memory and enable higher batch throughput.
- Result: ~1.8–2.9% drop on our summarization anchor set (macro avg rouge-L), larger drop on prompts with long prefix/state (>1k tokens).
- Throughput: token/sec improved 28% on p4d-like instances after kernel fusion. Cost/unit estimate down ~22% in simulated traces.
- Blocker: behavior mismatch between native CPU-eval harness and the runtime-in-the-loop eval (we see lower drop when running pure PyTorch quant sim vs runtime).

2) What we actually ran (quick log)
- run qexp_20260322_kv4_sym: 4-bit symmetric per-tensor quant for weights, KV cached as int4 with packing; seed 42; batch sizes 1/4/8; eval on anchor-1 (10k prompts subset)
  - notes: packing library needed tweak to handle odd-length sequences — fixed by Evan (PR #987).
- run qexp_20260323_asym-head: asymmetric per-head scale + bias correction on attention (attempt to recover head-wise variance).
- run qexp_20260324_fallback-8bit: hybrid path where prefix uses 8-bit KVs then switches to 4-bit for generation.

3) Observed diffs (detailed)
- Anchor summarization set: baseline ROUGE-L = 47.9, qexp_20260322 = 46.7 (drop 1.2 abs / 2.5% rel), qexp_20260323 = 46.2 (drop 1.7 abs / 3.6% rel).
- Long-prefix failure set (hand-curated 250 cases): failure rate (hallucination/omission) up from 4.4% -> 7.9% on qexp_20260323. Most failures happen when a crucial named-entity appears only in prefix KV and retrieval misses due to quant noise.
- Latency P95 unchanged for single-request path; throughput for steady-state generation (streaming) improved for large batches.

4) Hypotheses for regression
- per-head asymmetric scaling introduces bias on low-norm heads leading to attention misrouting when key distribution is heavy-tailed in prefix region.
- packing + alignment edge-case in runtime unpacks slightly differently than simulator causing off-by-one in attention index for some sequences. Evan found an unpack path difference — needs more tests.
- the fallback path (8-bit prefix) suggests we can recover correctness but at cost of throughput; maybe adaptive policy (detect long prefix / entity-heavy prompts) and route to fallback dynamically.

5) Immediate next experiments (priority order)
- exp A: repeat qexp_20260323 with deterministic unpack unit tests and instrument attention weights at top-k heads for the 250 long-prefix failures (owner: Evan, due: 2026-03-26).
- exp B: micro-bench of per-head scale clamp (cap scales to min 0.08) to see if stabilizes low-norm heads (owner: Tomás, due: 2026-03-28).
- exp C: hybrid runtime fallback policy prototype — route to 8-bit prefix only when prefix token count > 1024 OR when prompt contains >3 named entities (NER quick scan) (owner: Maya + Noah, prototype due: 2026-04-02).
- exp D: evaluation harness parity test — run same batch through (1) PyTorch quant sim, (2) runtime local container, (3) hosted dev staging to capture divergence points (owner: Aisha, due: 2026-03-27).

6) Short-term mitigations for onboarding customers
- If we onboard osprey-13B-ql into dedicated/dev tiers, gate 4-bit quant as opt-in only and keep default model variant at 8-bit. Add release note: "4-bit experimental: expect small regression on long-prefix summarization".
- Add automated canary that runs the 250 long-prefix cases on each model build and fails rollout if failure rate increases by >2% absolute. (Action: product / rollout infra ticket)

7) Engineering/infra notes (implementation friction)
- Packing lib: fixed unpacker PR merged but needs stress tests on odd-odd sequence lengths; we saw ~12 failing cases across random seed universe.
- CI: heavy eval runs are noisy on shared CI GPUs; recommend spinning up ephemeral infra for large evals to get stable results (ticket created: AI-7420).
- Telemetry: need to capture per-head attention variance in runtime traces; currently we capture token-level logits and sparse traces but not full head stats. Low priority but helpful for root cause.

8) Prompts / eval details (repro instructions)
- Anchor set location: s3://redwood-evals/anchors/summarization-anchor-2026-02-15.tar.gz
- Short reproducer: run python tools/eval_run.py --model osprey-13B-ql --quant-profile qexp_20260323 --input samples/long_prefix_250.json --metrics rouge-l 
- Experiment metadata: stored under experiments/qbench/2026/03/qexp_20260323_meta.json (internal bucket).

9) Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Is there a cheaper heuristic to detect entity-dependent prompts other than a full NER pipeline? Maybe a token-frequency entropy signal from prefix.
- How tolerant are customer applications to 2–3% summarization ROUGE drop if cost is reduced 20%? Need product to surface use-case sensitivity (action: product outreach).
- Are failures concentrated on specific attention heads (i.e., only 3 heads causing most regressions)? If yes, we might zero-out or stable-quant those heads.

10) Action items recap (owners + dates)
- Evan: deterministic unpack unit tests + instrumented attention traces (due 2026-03-26)
- Tomás: per-head clamp microbench (due 2026-03-28)
- Aisha: eval harness parity runs on staging (due 2026-03-27)
- Maya + Noah: fallback routing prototype (due 2026-04-02)
- Product: gating plan + customer comm brief for experimental 4-bit variant (requested by 2026-03-30)

Misc notes (informal):
- "Notes to self: we should add a short cookbook entry for \"when quantization hurts summarization\" — quick checklist for solutions (fallback, clamp head scales, targeted 8-bit)."
- Observed weirdness: a single case where changing seed flips between pass/fail on qexp_20260323 -> indicates instability: add repeated-seed runs to capture variance.

End of capture. Will update after exp A/B/C results come in.

Related links and artifacts listed above. If you want me to split this into a more formal runbook (with commands and CI jobs) I can make a follow-up doc — marking as draft for now.

-- Maya
